questions.solution:

11 × 12 = 132

132 × 11 = 1452

So, the pattern is: n × (n + 1) × n.

Apply the same rule for 12

12 × 13 = 156

156 × 12 = 1872

Thus, the missing number is 1872.

Hence, the correct option is "Option 1".

questions.question: Which of the following is a key requirement for admissibility of an electronic record under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), even if it's a secondary evidence?

options.text: It must be handwritten and notarized
It must be part of a hard drive submitted to court
It must be published in the Gazette
It must be accompanied by a certificate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It must be accompanied by a certificate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• Under the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (Indian Evidence Act), 1872**, electronic records can be considered admissible as evidence only if they meet certain conditions.

• The **certificate requirement** is specified under **Section 65B(4)** of the Act, which mandates that a certificate must accompany any electronic record submitted as secondary evidence.

• This certificate must include details about the electronic device used to produce the record, confirming its authenticity and the method by which the data was generated.

• The certificate is typically issued by a person in charge of the device (like a system administrator) and must be signed, providing assurance that the electronic record has not been tampered with.

• Without this certificate, the electronic record cannot be admitted as secondary evidence, even if it is relevant to the case.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act:**

• This section deals with the admissibility of electronic records as evidence in legal proceedings.

• It specifies that for electronic records to be admissible, they must meet the conditions outlined in the section, including the requirement of a certificate under **Sub-section 4**.

• This provision ensures that the integrity and reliability of electronic evidence are maintained.

• **Purpose of the Certificate:**

• The certificate serves as a safeguard against forgery, manipulation, or alteration of electronic records.

• It confirms that the information in the electronic record was produced by a reliable device and process.

• It provides details about the person responsible for the operation of the device and the accuracy of the record.

• **Other Relevant Provisions:**

• **Section 65A:** Introduces the concept of electronic records as evidence under specific circumstances.

• **Section 3:** Defines the term "evidence" to include all documents, including electronic records, produced for the inspection of the court.

• **Section 67A:** Discusses the proof of digital signatures and their verification.

• **Examples of Admissible Electronic Records:**

• Emails, text messages, and chat logs accompanied by a valid Section 65B certificate.

• Printed copies of financial records generated from computer systems with an authenticated certificate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Relevance of Electronic Records:** With the rise of digital transactions, electronic records have become crucial in legal cases involving contracts, financial transactions, and communications.

• **Judicial Precedent:** In the landmark judgment **Anvar P.V. vs. P.K. Basheer (2014)**, the Supreme Court of India ruled that electronic records without a Section 65B certificate are inadmissible as evidence.

• **Global Practices:** Many countries, including the **United States** and **United Kingdom**, have similar provisions for the admissibility of electronic evidence to ensure its reliability and authenticity.

• **Exceptions:** If the electronic record is presented as primary evidence (e.g., the original hard drive or device), the certificate requirement may not apply.

``

questions.question: Which of the following best characterizes the Mathura school of Buddhist art and architecture?

options.text: Use of sandstone and floral arches

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indigenous features with Yaksha influence**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Mathura School of Buddhist Art**, which thrived during the Kushan period (1st century CE to 3rd century CE), is characterized by **indigenous artistic traditions** with strong influences of **Yaksha and Yakshi iconography**. 
• Unlike the Gandhara School, which exhibited **Hellenistic features**, the Mathura School evolved from local traditions and prominently displayed **Indian motifs, techniques, and cultural themes**. 
• The Yaksha influence is evident in the **robust and cheerful figures** of Buddha and Bodhisattvas, which were depicted as wearing **simple drapery and adorned with ornaments**. 
• Mathura sculptures were primarily made of **red sandstone**, which was locally available and had a smooth finish. This material contributed to the unique aesthetic of the Mathura art style. 
• Mathura artists developed the concept of **anthropomorphic representations** of Buddha, marking a significant departure from earlier symbolic depictions like stupas or footprints. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Comparison with Gandhara School:** 
• The **Gandhara School**, which developed in present-day Pakistan and Afghanistan, is known for its **Greco-Roman influence**. It used **grey schist stone** and displayed features like curly hair, realistic anatomy, and flowing drapery. 
• In contrast, the Mathura School focused on **Indian traditions** and emphasized cheerful expressions and indigenous themes. 
• **Yaksha Influence in Indian Art:** 
• Yakshas and Yakshis are ancient nature spirits associated with fertility, abundance, and protection. Their statues often depicted **rounded, corpulent figures** with lively expressions. 
• The Mathura School adopted these stylistic features to create Buddha and Bodhisattva figures that emphasized **spiritual vitality**. 
• **Significance of Red Sandstone:** 
• Red sandstone was widely used by Mathura artists due to its **local availability**. The smooth and durable nature of the stone allowed intricate carvings and polished finishes. 
• This material distinguished Mathura sculptures from those of the Gandhara School, which predominantly used grey schist stone. 
• **Evolution of Anthropomorphic Buddha:** 
• The Mathura School played a crucial role in transitioning from symbolic representations of Buddha (like stupas, wheels, or footprints) to **anthropomorphic depictions**. 
• Buddha statues from Mathura often depicted him in a seated or standing posture, with a serene expression and a **halo behind his head**. 
• **Cultural Impact:** 
• The Mathura School influenced later Indian art forms, including the Gupta period, which is considered the **Golden Age** of Indian art and architecture. 
• Its emphasis on indigenous themes and techniques contributed to the **uniquely Indian identity** of Buddhist art. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Historical Context:** 
• The Mathura School flourished under **Kushan rulers**, who were patrons of art and architecture. Their support facilitated the development of Buddhist art in Mathura. 
• Mathura was an important center for religious and cultural activities during this period, contributing to its prominence in artistic innovations. 
• **Examples of Mathura Art:** 
• Iconic Buddha sculptures with distinct features like a **halo, urna (mark on the forehead), and elongated ears**. 
• Yaksha statues and images of Hindu deities, which showcased the versatility of Mathura artists. 
• **Legacy:** 
• The artistic traditions of the Mathura School influenced subsequent developments in Indian art, especially during the **Gupta period**. 
• Its emphasis on indigenous elements established a foundation for the evolution of Indian artistic identity. </ul

questions.question: The Pola festival, celebrated in the Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh, is dedicated to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bull worship**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Pola festival** is a significant cultural celebration dedicated to **bull worship** in the **Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh** and other parts of India.

• The festival is primarily celebrated by **farmers** to honor and express gratitude to their bulls, which are considered essential for agricultural activities such as plowing and transportation.

• **On the day of Pola**, bulls are bathed, decorated with ornaments, and worshipped. Farmers apply turmeric, oil, and colorful patterns to their bulls as a mark of respect.

• The festival includes **processions**, where bulls are paraded, and cultural activities such as bull races are organized in villages.

• This tradition symbolizes the deep connection between humans and animals in agrarian societies and showcases the importance of bulls in rural livelihoods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **About Pola Festival:**

• The Pola festival is celebrated during the **month of Shravan (August-September)** as per the Hindu calendar.

• The term "Pola" is derived from the Marathi language and is widely celebrated in states like **Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Chhattisgarh**.

• On this day, farmers abstain from agricultural work to give their bulls a day of rest and celebration.

• **Significance of Bull Worship:**

• Bulls are considered the backbone of traditional farming in India, especially in rural areas where mechanized farming is less prevalent.

• Worshipping bulls signifies acknowledging their **labor, loyalty, and contribution** to agricultural productivity.

• The festival also emphasizes the harmonious coexistence and respect between humans and animals.

• **Cultural Activities:**

• Farmers organize various events such as **bullock cart races, bull decoration competitions, and cultural performances**.

• Children often play with wooden bull toys called **Nandi Bail** as part of the festivities.

• Communities come together to share meals, celebrate, and strengthen social bonds.

• **Other Related Festivals:**

• **Makar Sankranti:** Another agrarian festival celebrated across India to honor cattle and the harvest season.

• **Mattu Pongal:** Celebrated in Tamil Nadu, this festival is dedicated to cattle worship and is part of the Pongal celebrations.

• **Gaijatra:** Celebrated in Nepal, it involves processions with cows to commemorate the deceased and honor cattle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Option 1 (Cow Worship):** While cows are also revered in Indian culture, the Pola festival specifically focuses on **bull worship**, not cows.

• **Option 2 (Rain Prayer):** Rain-related rituals and festivals like **Varsha Mangalam** or **Indra Puja** are distinct from Pola.

• **Option 4 (Harvest Sale):** Harvest festivals like **Lohri, Baisakhi, and Onam** celebrate the bounty of crops and are unrelated to the theme of Pola.

• The Pola festival uniquely celebrates the contribution of bulls to farming, distinguishing it from other agrarian or religious festivals.

• Brahmi is regarded as one of the **oldest writing scripts in India**, and it served as the precursor to many modern Indian scripts, including Devanagari. 
• The script was utilized for **Prakrit**, the lingua franca of the time, which made Asoka's messages accessible to the majority of the population. 
• Some inscriptions in the northwestern part of the empire were written in the **Kharosthi script**, but Brahmi remained the primary script for most regions under Asoka's rule.

• Brahmi is an **abugida**, meaning that each character represents a consonant with an inherent vowel sound. 
• It is believed to have been in use from the **3rd century BCE** to the **5th century CE**, evolving into various regional scripts. 
• The script was written from left to right, a characteristic that distinguishes it from Kharosthi, which was written from right to left. 
• Brahmi inscriptions are not limited to Asoka's reign; they are found in various historical sites like **Sanchi, Bharhut**, and **Ajanta**. 
• **Kharosthi Script**: 
• Kharosthi was predominantly used in the northwestern regions of Asoka's empire, including modern-day Pakistan and Afghanistan. 
• It was derived from the Aramaic script and was used for writing **Prakrit** and Gandhari languages. 
• Unlike Brahmi, Kharosthi was written from right to left.

• **Devanagari Script**: 
• Devanagari is a descendant of Brahmi and is one of the most widely used scripts in modern India. 
• It is used for writing languages like **Sanskrit, Hindi, Marathi, and Nepali**. 
• Devanagari evolved significantly after Asoka's time and was not used for his inscriptions. 
• **Tamil Script**: 
• The Tamil script is primarily used for writing the Tamil language and is not related to the inscriptions of Asoka. 
• It evolved independently in southern India and has a distinct structure compared to Brahmi.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about factors affecting the Money Multiplier (MM) **is/are correct**?

1. Cash held by individuals acts as a leakage and reduces the money multiplier.

2. Higher reserves held by banks with the RBI increase the money multiplier.

3. A higher Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) reduces the banking system's capacity to create money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Cash held by individuals acts as a leakage and reduces the money multiplier:** When individuals hold cash instead of depositing it in banks, it reduces the funds available for banks to lend. This reduces the capacity of the banking system to create credit, thereby lowering the **Money Multiplier (MM)**. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*

• **Higher reserves held by banks with the RBI:** When banks hold higher reserves with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), it reduces the funds available for lending. However, the statement incorrectly claims that it increases the money multiplier. In reality, higher reserves restrict the money creation process, which decreases the MM. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*

• **Higher Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) reduces the banking system's capacity to create money:** CRR is the percentage of a bank's total deposits that must be kept as reserves with the RBI. A higher CRR reduces the funds available for lending, thereby reducing the money multiplier. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*

• **Correct Option:** Only statements 1 and 3 are correct, making the correct answer **Only 1 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__

• **Money Multiplier (MM):**

• The money multiplier measures the maximum amount of money that banks can create with a given level of reserves. It is mathematically expressed as **MM = 1/Reserve Ratio**.

• It represents the relationship between the monetary base (currency + reserves) and the total money supply.

• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR):**

• CRR is a regulatory requirement imposed by the RBI on banks to maintain a certain percentage of their deposits as reserves with the central bank.

• CRR affects the liquidity in the banking system and directly influences the money creation process.

• **Factors Affecting the Money Multiplier:**

• **Public's Preference for Cash:** If people prefer to hold more cash, the funds available for banks to lend decrease, reducing the MM.

• **Reserve Requirements:** Higher reserve requirements (CRR or Statutory Liquidity Ratio) reduce the banking system's capacity to create credit, lowering the MM.

• **Economic Environment:** In times of economic uncertainty, banks may adopt a more cautious approach, holding higher reserves and lending less, which reduces the MM.

• **Role of RBI in Money Supply:**

• The RBI regulates the money supply through tools such as CRR, Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), and Open Market Operations (OMO).

• By adjusting reserve requirements, the RBI can influence the MM and the availability of credit in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Example of Money Multiplier:**

• If the reserve ratio is 10%, the money multiplier is **1/0.10 = 10**. This means every ₹1 in reserves can support ₹10 in total deposits.

• **Impact of Excess Reserves:**

• Banks may choose to hold excess reserves to mitigate risks, especially during economic downturns. This reduces the MM as fewer funds are available for lending.

• **Global Comparison:**

• Countries with lower reserve requirements typically have higher money multipliers, leading to greater credit creation capacity.

questions.question: Which sectors were largely excluded from industrial licensing after 1991?

 __ 
• In **1991**, India underwent significant economic reforms, marking the beginning of **economic liberalization**, which aimed to reduce government control over industries and encourage private sector participation. 
• As part of these reforms, the **industrial licensing system** was largely dismantled to promote ease of doing business, except for a few sectors due to their critical nature or social impact. 
• The sectors that remained under licensing included **alcohol, cigarettes, and explosives**, as they are either considered **socially sensitive** or pose **security concerns**. 
• **Alcohol:** Licensing remains due to its regulation under state excise laws and its implications on health and social behavior. 
• **Cigarettes:** Licensing is required due to public health concerns, as tobacco use is a leading cause of preventable deaths in India. 
• **Explosives:** Licensing is essential for safety and security reasons, as the misuse of explosives can lead to severe consequences. 
• Other sectors, such as **defense** and **telecom**, required licensing until reforms in later years, but they were not included in the initial exclusions post-1991. 
• The removal of licensing requirements for most sectors contributed significantly to India's rapid industrial growth and integration into the global economy. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __

• This policy was a landmark decision by the Government of India under the leadership of **Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.

• It introduced measures such as **abolishing industrial licensing** for most industries, reducing import tariffs, and removing export restrictions. 
• **Exceptions to Licensing:** 
• While most industries were freed from licensing, certain sectors remained controlled due to **national security**, **public health**, or **environmental concerns**. 
• These sectors included **alcohol, tobacco products (such as cigarettes), explosives, defense equipment, and hazardous chemicals**. 
• In these sectors, stringent licensing requirements ensured that production and distribution were **regulated** to prevent misuse or adverse social impacts. 
• **Impact of Liberalization:** 
• The reforms of 1991 led to **higher economic growth rates**, increased foreign investments, and the emergence of India as a **global economic power**. 
• It allowed private companies to compete with state-owned enterprises, leading to better efficiency, innovation, and customer services. 
• The removal of licensing also helped reduce bureaucratic red tape, improving India's **Ease of Doing Business** rankings. 
• **Key Characteristics of Excluded Sectors:** 
• **Alcohol:** Includes the production of liquor and spirits, which are regulated under state excise laws. Their consumption is taxed heavily and controlled due to health and social concerns. 
• **Cigarettes:** Involves tobacco products heavily regulated due to their association with diseases such as cancer and their impact on public health. 
• **Explosives:** Includes materials used for construction, mining, or defense purposes. Strict licensing is mandatory to ensure safety and prevent misuse in criminal or terrorist activities.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is TRUE for Whole Numbers?

options.text: They include zero and positive integers.

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Whole numbers are simply the set of natural numbers (counting numbers) along with zero.

Set of Whole Numbers (W) = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, ...}

This means they include zero and all positive integers, but no fractions or negative numbers.

**∴ The correct answer is They include zero and positive integers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Checking all the given statements:**

⇒ Option 1: They include fractions. (False, fractions like 1/2 or 3/4 are Rational Numbers, not Whole Numbers)

⇒ Option 2: They include negative numbers. (False, negative numbers like −1 or −5 belong to Integers, not Whole Numbers)

⇒ Option 4: They start from 1. (False, numbers starting from 1 are called Natural Numbers)

⇒ Option 3: They include zero and positive integers. (True)

**Derivation:**

⇒ The set of Whole Numbers is mathematically denoted by W.

⇒ W = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, ...}

⇒ The numbers {1, 2, 3, 4, ...} are positive integers.

⇒ Therefore, Whole Numbers = {0} + Positive Integers.

**∴ The correct answer is They include zero and positive integers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Natural Numbers (N)

These are the counting numbers starting from 1. N = {1, 2, 3, 4, ...}. They do not include zero, negative numbers, or fractions.

Integers (Z)

This set includes all whole numbers and their negative counterparts. Z = {..., −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...}.

Rational Numbers (Q)

Any number that can be expressed in the form of p/q, where p and q are integers and q is not equal to zero. It includes fractions, terminating decimals, and repeating decimals.

Real Numbers (R)

The set of all rational and irrational numbers. They represent all possible continuous points on the number line.

questions.question: A', 'B', and 'C' formed a consulting firm. Their capital investments were Rs. 6,00,000, Rs. 4,00,000, and Rs. 5,00,000, respectively. After 3 months, 'A' withdrew Rs. 1,00,000, and 'B' added Rs. 1,00,000. The partnership lasted for 9 months. What was the ratio of their effective capital contributions?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective Capital = Capital × Time

A's effective capital = (6 × 3) + (5 × 6) = 18 + 30 = 48

B's effective capital = (4 × 3) + (5 × 6) = 12 + 30 = 42

C's effective capital = 5 × 9 = 45

Ratio = 48 : 42 : 45 = 16 : 14 : 15

**∴ The correct answer is 16:14:15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

After 3 months: A withdrew Rs. 1,00,000; B added Rs. 1,00,000

Total time of partnership = 9 months

**Formula Used:**

Ratio of Profit = Ratio of Effective Capital = (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂) : (C₃ × T₃)

 A 6L × 3m 5L × 6m B 4L × 3m 5L × 6m C 5L × 9m 
• 0 3 Months 9 Months 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A's investment for first 3 months = Rs. 6,00,000

⇒ A's investment for remaining 6 months = 6,00,000 − 1,00,000 = Rs. 5,00,000

⇒ A's effective capital = (6,00,000 × 3) + (5,00,000 × 6) = 18,00,000 + 30,00,000 = Rs. 48,00,000

 

⇒ B's investment for first 3 months = Rs. 4,00,000

⇒ B's investment for remaining 6 months = 4,00,000 + 1,00,000 = Rs. 5,00,000

⇒ B's effective capital = (4,00,000 × 3) + (5,00,000 × 6) = 12,00,000 + 30,00,000 = Rs. 42,00,000

 

⇒ C's investment for entire 9 months = Rs. 5,00,000

⇒ C's effective capital = 5,00,000 × 9 = Rs. 45,00,000

 

⇒ Ratio of their effective capitals = 48,00,000 : 42,00,000 : 45,00,000

⇒ Canceling 1,00,000 from all terms, Ratio = 48 : 42 : 45

⇒ Dividing by 3, Ratio = 16 : 14 : 15

**∴ The correct answer is 16:14:15.**

Simple Partnership

When all partners invest their capital for the exact same period, profits are distributed strictly in the ratio of their original investments.

Compound Partnership

When partners invest different amounts for different time periods, profits are distributed in the ratio of their effective capitals (calculated as Capital × Time).

Active and Sleeping Partners

An active partner receives a fixed salary or a certain percentage of total profit for managing the business operations, while the remaining profit is shared among all partners according to their effective capital ratios.

questions.question: The price of a product is decreased by x% and then increased by x%. The final price becomes 10% less than the original. What is the value of x (approximately)?

When a value is first decreased by x% and then increased by x%, the net change is always a decrease of (x² ÷ 100)%.

Given the net decrease is 10%:

⇒ x² ÷ 100 = 10

⇒ x² = 1000

⇒ x = √1000 ≈ 31.62

**∴ The correct answer is 31.6.**

Initial decrease in price = x%

Subsequent increase in price = x%

Final price is 10% less than the original price.

Net percentage change for successive changes a% and b% = (a + b + a × b ÷ 100)%

**Calculation:**

 Original Price 100

⇒ Let the original price be 100.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: Net Change = (a + b + a × b ÷ 100)%. Use a positive sign for an increase and a negative sign for a decrease.

Equal Increase and Decrease

If a quantity is increased by x% and subsequently decreased by the same x%, or vice versa, the final value is always less than the original. The net percentage decrease is always exactly (x² ÷ 100)%.

Base Value Concept

Any percentage calculation is computed on a reference base value. When multiple percentage changes occur sequentially, the intermediate value immediately becomes the new base for the next percentage calculation.

questions.question: A man got 10% of his investment as profit. If he invested Rs. 5000, and the profit was reinvested, what will be the total value after the second year with the same profit rate?
